images.title: Find backend resources and their circuit-breaker status
images.alt: Azure Portal Backends tab showing backend type and Enabled or Disabled circuit-breaker status. Backend names, descriptions, and runtime URLs are blacked out.
images.caption: The Backends tab lists individual backend resources; Load balancer is a separate tab. This is an existing mixed-backend inventory, not the two-backend pool deployed in the article. Backend names, descriptions, and runtime endpoints are redacted.

images.title: Locate the system-assigned identity and role-assignment entry point
images.navigation: API Management service > Security > Managed identities > System assigned
images.alt: Azure Portal System assigned managed identity settings with Status On, a redacted Object principal ID field, and the Azure role assignments button.
images.caption: The identity was already On. Its principal ID is redacted. This screen identifies the APIM identity and provides a role-assignment entry point; it does not prove that the required role exists on any Foundry account. No toggle or role assignment was changed.

images.title: Inspect backend circuit-breaker fields without confusing them with policy retries
images.navigation: API Management service > APIs > Backends > select backend > Circuit breaker settings > select rule
images.alt: Existing circuit-breaker edit form showing failure count 1, interval 2 seconds, status ranges 429 and 500 through 503, trip duration 30 seconds, and Retry-After True Accept. Rule name is redacted.
images.caption: Read-only inspection of an existing rule: count 1, interval 2 seconds, status codes 429 and 500-503, trip duration 30 seconds, and Retry-After accepted. These are not the article's 429-only sample defaults. A backend circuit breaker and the operation policy's retry block are separate mechanisms. Save was not clicked.
